segments.title: Opening: location and start of recording
segments.summary: Bill Russell sets up the recording at Israel Gorman's home and Gorman gives his name.

segments.title: Albert-system clarinets and Willie Humphrey
segments.summary: Gorman describes Albert-system clarinets and how Willie Humphrey struggled with his horn.

segments.title: Gorman's melodic style and playing close to the tune
segments.summary: Gorman describes staying close to the melody in small bands and his professor's advice about thirds and fifths.

segments.title: Recording March of the Bobcat with Albert Elkhorn
segments.summary: Gorman and the interviewer recall recording numbers together with a young man from Switzerland, and never hearing from him afterward.

segments.title: Lorenzo Tio's clarinet tone, compared to Benny Goodman
segments.summary: Gorman describes Tio's clean, medium-volume tone and how he stood while teaching.

segments.title: Tio's lessons: duets and figuring out music
segments.summary: Gorman recounts Tio's duets with pupils and his view of working out music like counting money.

segments.title: Tio's teaching: counting divisions and 'stealing' notes
segments.summary: Gorman recalls Tio's advice that musicians steal time from notes, how to count eighth and sixteenth divisions, and Tio's foot-patting.

segments.title: Practicing long notes to build tone and lip
segments.summary: Gorman explains long-note and scale practice to build the lip muscle.

segments.title: Reeds: Buffet cane, plastic, and caring for his horn
segments.summary: Gorman tells of French cane reeds, the switch to plastic reeds via Peterson's music store, reed life, and washing his horn nightly.

segments.title: Tio and others needing only one clarinet
segments.summary: Gorman and the interviewer discuss the E-flat and B-flat clarinets Tio and Bechet-era players carried, and Tio needing only one horn.

segments.title: Knowing your keys: Tio's advice, Big Eye Louis and the C clarinet
segments.summary: Gorman recounts Tio's advice to know your keys, then discusses Big Eye Louis Nelson and Pill playing C clarinet and faltering on B-flat.

segments.title: Playing E-flat clarinet in brass bands
segments.summary: Gorman lists brass bands he played E-flat clarinet with, including Celestin's Tuxedo, Chris Kelly and Young Tuxedo, and why he liked the instrument.

segments.title: Pensacola job with Buddy Petit and the band
segments.summary: Gorman describes the two-year contract in Pensacola with Buddy Petit's band for an undertaker, its members, and the odd Carl Fischer saxophone.

segments.title: Teaching himself saxophone in Pensacola
segments.summary: Gorman explains how he practiced the saxophone while the others went out, and was soon playing it on the job.

segments.title: Request for a portrait of Buddy Petit
segments.summary: The interviewer asks Gorman about how Buddy Petit played and what he was like personally.
